hero.blurb: A Claude Code kit that interviews you, plans the project, writes its rules and memory, and builds a working skeleton with CI.

arch.alt: How setup works: you give a brief or answer 9 questions and approve the plan; SETUP_PROMPT.txt drives Claude Code through phases A to F (interview and propose, docs and rules, version research, skeleton and verify); the result is rules and memory, a .claude folder with commands, agents and hooks, and a skeleton with make check and CI.
arch.title: One prompt, six phases.
arch.footnote: When setup finishes, _kit/ is deleted: only adapted files stay, and every later session starts with /start-session.

capabilities.alt: Four things the kit gives every project: session memory, a gateway per outside service, reviewer agents, and a check gate Claude must pass before it finishes.
capabilities.title: Built to keep going.

items.title: It remembers between sessions
items.does: Reads PROGRESS and the INCIDENTS lessons, checks git, then proposes 3–6 small tasks before any code.

items.title: One gateway per outside service
items.does: A provider file, a mapper, a config line and contract tests. Callers never change.

items.title: Reviewers before commits
items.does: Architecture, security and UI reviewers check the diff against the rulebook and rank findings.

items.title: Quality gates from day one
items.does: Before Claude ends a turn, make check runs lint, types, boundaries and tests. Red sends it back.

decisions.alt: Five design decisions: plan before code, memory lives in the repo, every outside service behind a gateway, versions researched not guessed, the kit deletes itself.
decisions.title: Why it works this way.
items: Setup writes the plan, the rules and an empty-but-working skeleton only. No feature code until you approve a phased roadmap that tackles the riskiest unknown first.
PROGRESS, INCIDENTS and ADRs are plain Markdown the agent reads at the start of every session, so context survives restarts and new chats.
Every outside service behind a gateway
Providers stay private. Selection, fallback, caching, rate limits and retries live in one gateway per domain, so adding or swapping a provider never touches callers.
Phase D picks the newest set of versions that are officially compatible with each other, checked against registries and release notes, and records it in ADR 0003.
_kit/ is a template, not part of your repo. After setup only adapted files remain, and the kit improves on its own as you learn lessons that apply everywhere.

stack.alt: Stack rule-sets included: Android with Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Hilt and Room; Python API with FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy and uv; Web with Next.js, React and Tailwind; Node API with TypeScript, Fastify and Zod.
